source.section: PIT-ADJ instructions PDF page 4, line 13; PDF page 5, Table 1; PIT-ADJ instructions PDF page 1, line 1; PDF page 2, line 7; Form PIT-1 lines 9 to 18 and 22; instructions PDF page 25, line 12; PIT-1 instructions PDF page 25, line 14; PDF page 26, Low- and Middle-Income Tax Exemption Worksheet lines 1 to 8; PDF page 22, line 5; Tax Rate Table PDF pages 1 to 6, rows; PDF page 7 (T-7), over 100,000

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = private pension (person 0) 28,000.00 = 28,000.00. Federal taxable income = 28,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 - 1 x 1,600.00 additional for age 65 or older = -5,100.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Form PIT-1 takes only the federal line 12 amount, and no line for what the federal return subtracts after line 12). Form PIT-1, married filing jointly. Line 9 federal AGI 28,000.00. Line 10 0.00 (standard deduction taken). Line 11 additions, PIT-ADJ line 1 (all state and municipal bond interest left out of federal AGI): other states' bond interest 40,000.00 = 40,000.00. Line 12 federal standard deduction 33,100.00. Line 13 dependents 0.00. Line 14 low- and middle-income worksheet: line 1 28,000.00; line 2 30,000.00; line 3 0.00; line 4 0.10; line 5 0.00; line 6 2,500.00 - 0.00 = 2,500.00; line 7 2 exemption(s); line 8 = 5,000.00. Line 15, PIT-ADJ: line 13 age 65 or older: Table 1 (married filing jointly) row for federal AGI 28,000.00 gives 8,000.00 x 1 qualifying = 8,000.00; PIT-ADJ line 28 total 8,000.00. Line 17 = 28,000.00 + 40,000.00 - 33,100.00 - 5,000.00 - 8,000.00 = 21,900.00. Federal AGI less the federal deduction is -5,100.00 here; the form subtracts the whole line 12 amount, so that negative figure carries through its arithmetic. By the projection: state_agi = federal taxable income -5,100.00 + 40,000.00 = 34,900.00; less base deductions 13,000.00 gives 21,900.00. Line 18 tax, schedule as numbers: 1.5% x 8,000.00 = 120 + 3.2% x 13,900.00 = 444.8; total 564.8, to the cent 564.80. The table row over 21,800 to 21,900 gives 563; expected keeps the formula figure. Lines 19 to 21 0.00. Line 22 net New Mexico income tax 564.80. Federal taxable income is entered as AGI less the deduction, negative, not 0: the form has no floor before line 17, so a 0 here would overstate New Mexico income by 5,100.00. Line 13's second example (AGI 28,000) gives 8,000 x 2 because the spouse there is blind; blindness is not_modelled, so one amount here.
